prompt: Explain how surface code quantum error correction handles bit flips.
preferred_response_yw: Surface code arranges qubits in a 2D grid with alternating X and Z stabilizer syndrome measurements, detecting and correcting bit-flip (X) errors through Z-stabilizer syndrome extraction without collapsing data superposition.
rejected_response_yl: Quantum error correction just copies the qubit three times like a classical parity check, which protects against all quantum noise.
